item.title: China-ASEAN expo to highlight FTA 3.0 opportunities
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-17
NANNING, Sept. 16 (Xinhua) -- The 23rd China-ASEAN Expo will spotlight new business opportunities under the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area (CAFTA) 3.0 framework, with more than 3,400 companies from over 70 countries and regions set to participate, event organizers said on Wednesday.
Scheduled to run from Sept. 17 to 21 in Nanning, capital of south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, the expo will cover about 170,000 square meters, showcasing the latest achievements in China-ASEAN cooperation.
Under the theme "CAFTA 3.0 Opportunities, Better Life," the expo will feature products and projects in areas ranging from traditional industries to digital communications, green development and artificial intelligence (AI).
A dedicated AI marketplace will display more than 500 products, while a new exhibition area will highlight demand from ASEAN countries for projects and applications in transport, smart logistics, AI, urban management and industrial park development.
Science and technology authorities and high-tech institutions from countries including Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand will send delegations to the expo.
Timor-Leste will participate for the first time as a full ASEAN member and a co-host of the expo, bringing all 11 ASEAN member states together in Nanning following the bloc's expansion.
Over 50 trade and investment promotion activities will also be held during the expo, focusing on trade and investment facilitation, regional economic integration, and cross-border industrial and supply chain cooperation.
China and ASEAN are working to accelerate the implementation of the CAFTA 3.0 Upgrade Protocol. Signed in October 2025, the protocol covers areas such as the digital economy and green development.
Economic ties between China and ASEAN have continued to deepen. Bilateral trade topped 1 trillion U.S. dollars for the first time in 2025, totaling 1.05 trillion dollars, up 7.4 percent year on year. In the first seven months of 2026, trade between the two sides reached 744.41 billion dollars, an increase of 24.7 percent year on year and accounting for 21.8 percent of China's total foreign trade.
China has remained ASEAN's largest trading partner for 17 consecutive years, while ASEAN has been China's largest trading partner for six successive years.

item.title: Chinese vice premier stresses opening up in western regions as Pinglu Canal opens
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-17
Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, attends a ceremony marking the Pinglu Canal's completion and opening to navigation in Qinzhou, south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, Sept. 16, 2026. (Xinhua/Liu Weibing)
NANNING, Sept. 16 (Xinhua) -- Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang on Wednesday underscored the importance of further opening up in China's western regions as the Pinglu Canal, a trade shortcut to Southeast Asia, officially opened in south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region.
Ding, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made his remarks at a ceremony in Qinzhou, announcing that after four years of hard work, the Pinglu Canal has been completed and is open to navigation.
He emphasized that the opening of the canal should be seized as an opportunity to develop a first-class international gateway port at the Beibu Gulf, expand opening-up in western regions, and contribute more significantly to building a new development pattern.
Built at a cost of 72.7 billion yuan (about 10.75 billion U.S. dollars), the 134.2-kilometer Pinglu Canal links Nanning, capital of Guangxi, with the Beibu Gulf.
Ding also boarded a vessel to inspect navigation operations and ecological protection along the canal. He pointed out that the Pinglu Canal, as key infrastructure for multimodal transport integrating river, rail and sea, is a backbone project of the New Western Land-Sea Corridor.
He called for sound operation and management and strengthening transport capacity support and cargo source organization, in order to fully leverage the advantages of coordinated maritime and land transport and internal and external connectivity. This will ensure the safe and efficient operation of this golden waterway linking inland areas and the sea, and achieve the organic unity of economic, social and ecological benefits, he added.
The canal provides key support for Guangxi in its efforts to utilize sea access and pursue open development, injecting new momentum into both enhanced connectivity between China and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations and the high-quality joint construction of the Belt and Road.

item.title: Xi stresses sustained efforts to expand, strengthen advanced manufacturing
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-17
BEIJING, Sept. 17 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has urged sustained efforts to expand and strengthen advanced manufacturing to provide strong support for advancing Chinese modernization.
Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks in a recent instruction, which was conveyed at a national conference on advanced manufacturing held in Beijing on Wednesday and Thursday.
Efforts should be made to ensure both high-quality development and greater security, pursue smart, green and integrated development, and make the country's industrial chains more self-supporting and risk-resilient, Xi stressed.
He emphasized the need to accelerate the development of a modernized industrial system with advanced manufacturing as the backbone, and reinforce the foundations of the real economy.

item.title: HKSAR chief executive: Hong Kong to play due part in making GBA world-class city cluster
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-17
John Lee (C), chief executive of the HKSAR, holds a press conference to take questions from reporters after delivering Hong Kong's first five-year plan and the 2026 Policy Address, September 16, 2026. /VCG
Hong Kong will participate in the development of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) into a world-class city cluster with global influence, John Lee, chief executive of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR), said on Wednesday.
Delivering Hong Kong's first five-year plan for economic and social development (2026-2030), Lee said that Hong Kong will contribute to developing an information and technology industry chain in the GBA. It will strive to invite more I&T leadership talent from the mainland and overseas to establish a presence in Hong Kong and facilitate the application of intellectual property rights arising from research and development outcomes.
Infrastructure is a major component of connectivity within the GBA. Lee said Hong Kong will advance the construction of cross-boundary rail links and expedite the formation of enormous intelligent computing clusters.
To further align rules and mechanisms in the GBA, efforts will be made to foster the mutual recognition of professional qualifications and promote the alignment of healthcare services and regulatory frameworks. The cross-boundary flow of people, goods, capital and data will be facilitated, said the blueprint, also putting the development of cross-boundary autonomous driving on the agenda.
In deepening exchanges between the residents of GBA cities, the plan listed measures to strengthen cooperation between universities, promote cross-boundary elderly services, jointly conserve biodiversity and achieve integrated development of culture, sports and tourism.

item.title: China's railway construction gains strong momentum as Jan.-Aug. investment rises
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-17
Actresses perform on the first high-speed train from Ruijin in east China's Jiangxi Province to Yan'an in northwest China's Shaanxi Province, Sept. 6, 2026. (Xinhua/Shao Rui)
BEIJING, Sept. 16 (Xinhua) -- China's railway construction endeavors maintained solid momentum in the first eight months of 2026, with significant progress made on a number of key projects, the national railway operator said on Wednesday.
Fixed-asset investment in the railway sector totaled 511.8 billion yuan (about 75.68 billion U.S. dollars) in the first eight months of the year, up 1.5 percent year on year, according to China State Railway Group Co., Ltd.
This steady progress in railway construction has helped boost related industries and employment, injecting new momentum into the expansion of domestic demand and stable economic growth, the company said.
A number of key projects have recently made positive progress. For instance, the Wenling-Yuhuan section of the Hangzhou-Shaoxing-Taizhou high-speed railway in east China's Zhejiang Province opened to traffic, putting Yuhuan, a city in southeastern Zhejiang, within 1 hour and 47 minutes of the provincial capital Hangzhou by direct high-speed train.
Construction also advanced on several technically challenging projects.
Railway construction teams have pushed tunnel construction forward in cold and difficult mountain terrain, finished tunnels through complex and risky ground conditions, started building beams on major railway bridges, and begun laying tracks on the country's longest high-speed railway bridge under construction.
The company said it will fully implement the railway construction tasks set out in the outline of the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), coordinate the planning and construction of new lines with the upgrading and capacity expansion of conventional railways, and continue to improve the quality and efficiency of railway investment to support high-quality economic and social development.
China has built the world's largest high-speed railway network. By the end of 2025, the country's total operating railway mileage had reached 165,000 km, including more than 50,000 km of high-speed rail.
According to the company, the country's operational railway mileage is expected to reach 180,000 km by 2030, with high-speed rail amounting to roughly 60,000 km.
Railway construction boasts a long industrial chain and wide spillover effects, driving demand for steel, cement, construction machinery and equipment manufacturing, while creating local jobs.
In the first seven months of the year, China's railways recorded 2.8 billion passenger trips, up 4.1 percent year on year and a record high for the period. Over the same timeframe, the network carried 14.85 million trips by foreign passengers, a surge of 32.5 percent.
China's railways carried 2.35 billion tonnes of cargo in the first seven months of 2026, rising 0.7 percent from a year earlier, lending solid support to logistics cost cuts and sustained stable economic performance.
Under national plans, China's high-speed rail network is projected to hit 70,000 km by 2035, featuring eight north-south vertical lines and eight east-west horizontal lines. When fully built, the network will cover major cities, city clusters and key economic zones across the country.

item.title: Pinglu Canal opens with wildlife bridge for safer animal crossings
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-17
The wildlife eco-bridge at the watershed section of the Pinglu Canal spans the navigable channel. /CMG
The 134.2-km-long Pinglu Canal in south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region officially opened to navigation on September 16, connecting the Xijiang River waterway with the Beibu Gulf.
Among the canal's 104 bridges is a special ecological overpass designed exclusively for wildlife, locally dubbed a "bridge of life."
The 240-meter-long, 20-meter-wide bridge is not open to vehicles and has no asphalt pavement. Instead, its deck is covered with 0.6 to 1.2 meters of planting soil and planted with native vegetation, including Chinese banyan and Quercus glauca, as well as fruit trees that provide food for wildlife.
Rock piles and water-collection pits have also been installed to recreate the natural conditions of the surrounding mountain forests, providing shade, food and hiding places for animals such as spotted linsangs, Asian leopard cats and red-bellied tree squirrels.
The ecological overpass is designed to provide a safe and natural passage for wildlife, helping maintain ecological connectivity along the canal.
Along the Pinglu Canal, 36 ecological conservation zones have also been established. Measures tailored to local conditions include installing artificial fish nests, erecting perches for birds and restoring wetlands, providing habitats and refuge for wildlife.
Pinglu Canal is China's first major nationally planned river-to-sea canal project since 1949, it can accommodate vessels of up to 5,000 tonnes. The canal is expected to shorten shipping between China's southwestern hinterland and ASEAN by 560 km and cut logistics costs by 18-30%.

item.title: Hong Kong unveils maiden 5-year plan, charts roadmap for high-quality development
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-17
John Lee, chief executive of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, unveils Hong Kong's first five-year plan for economic and social development (2026-2030) and delivers his fifth policy address in Hong Kong, south China, Sept. 16, 2026. (Xinhua/Chen Duo)
HONG KONG, Sept. 16 (Xinhua) -- The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) on Wednesday unveiled its first five-year plan for economic and social development (2026-2030), a milestone as it enters a new phase of becoming more prosperous.
The plan will help build a more open, inclusive, liberal, prosperous and safer Hong Kong, said HKSAR Chief Executive John Lee.
Unveiling the blueprint, Lee said the 2026-2030 period is five crucial years for Hong Kong to seize the opportunity to enhance social well-being and build a better home for all.
Comprising seven parts and 28 chapters, the plan sets out a total of 105 indicators spanning a wide range of areas. Key objectives include achieving new breakthroughs in economic development, boosting international competitiveness and influence, as well as significantly improving public well-being.
According to the plan, Hong Kong's real GDP growth rate is projected to remain within a reasonable range during the 2026-2030 period, while the value added of the tourism industry is expected to rise about 40 to 50 percent to 126 billion Hong Kong dollars (about 16.06 billion U.S. dollars) by 2030.
Hong Kong aims to elevate the ratio of total domestic expenditure on innovation activities to GDP to 3 after 2030, compared with a reading of 1.63 in 2024, the plan said.
To sharpen its competitive edge, Hong Kong plans to consolidate and enhance its status as an international financial, maritime and trade center, and develop itself into an international innovation and technology center and a global hub for high-caliber talent, according to the blueprint.
Efforts will also be made to expedite the development of the Northern Metropolis, deepen the development of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area and create an international collaboration network.
Social well-being has been high on the HKSAR government's agenda. While prioritizing young people's education, employment, entrepreneurship and home ownership, the government also pledged to eliminate substandard subdivided units by 2030. According to the plan, Hong Kong will supply 196,000 public flats in the coming five years, aiming to cut the average waiting time to under four years by 2030-31.
The document also underscored efforts to adopt a holistic approach to development and security, boost governance efficacy, and strengthen the institutional safeguards for implementation.
Delivering the policy address for 2026 shortly after presenting the blueprint, Lee said key policy initiatives and projects in the policy address will serve as core drivers to implement the five-year plan through enhanced inter-departmental coordination and regular progress reviews.
To better solicit public opinion on the city's future development, the HKSAR government held over 100 consultation sessions over the past three months, receiving over 17,000 submissions on the five-year plan and 11,000 on the policy address.
Noting this year marks the beginning of China's 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), Lee said that the inaugural blueprint represented a major initiative by the HKSAR government to uphold and enhance the executive-led system and improve governance efficacy.
The blueprint underscored the strategic need for Hong Kong to proactively align with national development strategies and better integrate into the overall national development, while also laying out an action agenda to promote Hong Kong's high-quality development, the chief executive said.
